description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related series (Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy) vary as a function of Initial Confidence. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.81 to 0.99 with tick labels shown at irregular intervals (including 0.81, 0.82, 0.84, 0.85, then continuing by about 0.01 up to 0.99). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0 with regularly spaced ticks at 0.2 intervals. The Final Accuracy series is a blue solid line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it starts near 1.00 at 0.81, stays mostly between about 0.88 and 0.97 across the range, dips to around 0.86 near 0.95, and ends near 0.98 at 0.99. The Δ Accuracy series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and error bars; it begins around 0.45 at 0.81, declines to roughly 0.32 by about 0.84, reaches a low near 0.14 around 0.86, rises to about 0.37 near 0.88, fluctuates mostly between about 0.14 and 0.30 through the mid-range, and finishes near 0.04 at 0.99. The Initial Accuracy series is a green dash-dot line with square markers and error bars; it starts around 0.54 at 0.81, varies upward and downward through the mid-range (including values around 0.75 near 0.86 and around 0.58 near 0.88), trends upward after about 0.93 (around 0.66–0.76 through 0.97), and ends near 0.94 at 0.99.
